chains.title: TFAP2A binding disruption at the enhancer reduces IRF6 regulation
chains.cell_type: Epidermal development is implicated in the literature; a specific cleft-relevant developmental cell type is not established by the supplied evidence.

links.claim: The literature reports that rs642961 abrogates AP2A binding, predicting stronger binding to ref A than alt G; no QBiC-SELEX result is supplied, and ENCODE reports no TFAP2A ChIP peak at the variant.
rs642961 lies in the enhancer-like cCRE EH38E2863563, also described in the literature as MCS9.7.
The literature reports that AP2A regulates MCS9.7 enhancer activity and IRF6 protein expression, supporting IRF6 as the proposed target.
The reported TFAP2A–MCS9.7–IRF6 regulatory relationship is in the context of epidermal development, but its operation in a specific cleft-relevant cell type is not shown here.
rs642961 is associated with orofacial clefts, but the supplied evidence does not prove that this TFAP2A–IRF6 mechanism causes the association.

predictions: In a relevant developmental cell model, the G allele should show less TFAP2A occupancy than A and should reduce IRF6 regulation through this element.
Perturbing or editing the element should affect IRF6 more consistently than UTP25 or TRAF3IP3.
falsified_if: A and G show no reproducible difference in TFAP2A binding in an appropriate assay, or editing the variant/element has no effect on IRF6 regulation in a relevant developmental model.

chains.title: No TF-mediated effect at rs642961
predictions: There is no reproducible TF-mediated allelic effect of rs642961 in a relevant developmental context; the cleft association could instead reflect linkage or another mechanism.
An allele-specific binding difference in an in vitro assay, if observed, would not by itself establish a regulatory effect in cells.
falsified_if: Editing A to G in a relevant developmental cell model reproducibly reduces TFAP2A occupancy and IRF6 expression, and restoring the binding or enhancer activity rescues the expression effect.

chains.title: TFAP2A binding disruption at the enhancer regulates TRAF3IP3 instead
chains.cell_type: A cleft-relevant developmental context is proposed but not established; the supplied TRAF3IP3 eQTL evidence is from blood-related tissues.

links.claim: The literature reports that rs642961 abrogates AP2A binding, predicting stronger binding to ref A than alt G; no QBiC-SELEX result is supplied, and ENCODE reports no TFAP2A ChIP peak at the variant.

TRAF3IP3 is a possible locus target based on locus-to-gene scores and blood-related eQTLs, but regulation by this cCRE is not demonstrated.

The variant/locus is associated with orofacial clefts, but no supplied evidence connects a TRAF3IP3 regulatory effect to that phenotype.

falsified_if: Element perturbation or variant editing affects IRF6 but not TRAF3IP3 in relevant cells, or there is no relevant-cell TFAP2A binding difference.
